clue.text: Insects react badly when colliding with posts

indicators.note: doing something badly scrambles it, so the letters of react are jumbled

parts.note: pillars are upright posts supporting a structure

explanation.surface: Some bugs get flustered when they bump into fence posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges REACT into CATER; 'when colliding with' simply puts PILLARS beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are larvae of butterflies and moths, the most familiar crawling insects of the garden.

clue.text: Worms can make wiggly line in shifting sand

indicators.note: one jumbled word is placed in the middle of the other jumbled word
shifting sand moves about, so its letters are rearranged
a wiggly line is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worms leave a squiggly trail as they burrow through drifting sand.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'wiggly' and 'shifting' are anagram signals, one per word; the jumbled line sits inside the jumbled sand. 'can make' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are the zoological phylum of segmented worms, earthworms and leeches among them.

clue.text: Eastern male married a girl

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
M is the abbreviation for married, as on forms and in genealogy

explanation.surface: An oriental gentleman has wed a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so it can stand for any girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: To scoff pie is naughty in a public building

indicators.note: letters that misbehave are out of their proper order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wolfing down a pie inside a government building is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A government-run branch selling stamps and handling mail, a public building on many high streets.

clue.text: Story to introduce the German songs

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second, introducing it

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A tale is told to present German songs.
explanation.walkthrough: DER is a masculine form of 'the' in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, the Romantic genre of Schubert and Schumann.

clue.text: Golf course where ace is seen at end of month

indicators.note: the letter for ace sits after the month, at its end

parts.note: August is a month of the year
A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A golf course where someone hits a hole in one as the month closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace' looks like golf's hole in one, but it is the playing-card A.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta National in Georgia, USA, is the famous course that hosts the Masters tournament.

clue.text: So " ether's part" could fancifully be this?

definitions.text: So " ether's part" could fancifully be this?

indicators.note: a fanciful rearrangement plays freely with the letters of the quoted words

parts.note: the possessive s is counted here as a real letter

explanation.surface: A whimsical suggestion that the upper sky is part of the ether.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually the 's of ether's supplies a letter. The whole clue also works as a definition: the upper atmosphere was once thought of as part of the ether.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmospheric layer above the troposphere, which old notions placed within the heavenly ether.

clue.text: Prepare herb for fixed amount of medicine

parts.note: to do food is to prepare it, as in doing the vegetables
sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: Get some herb ready to measure out a medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is the measured quantity of a drug to take, which is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Depressed women entertained by fellow

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts you inside their home, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A gloomy academic has female guests to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' means a college fellow, a DON, rather than just any man.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or dejected, a synonym in the sense of unhappy.

clue.text: Postboy possibly producing confusion — awfully green?

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion

indicators.note: something done awfully is botched, so the letters of green are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young postman is muddled and rather inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles the colour word, which is added after the confusion. 'possibly' marks the postboy as only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A postboy carried letters, one example of a courier who delivers messages.

clue.text: Was it lost when Mrs Hubbard failed to deliver?

definitions.text: Was it lost when Mrs Hubbard failed to deliver?

parts.words: Was it lost when Mrs Hubbard failed to deliver?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Old Mother Hubbard finds her cupboard bare and her dog gets no bone, so affection offered only for food would vanish

explanation.surface: Did the dog stop caring when Old Mother Hubbard brought him nothing?
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Hubbard is an English nursery rhyme: she went to the cupboard to fetch her poor dog a bone, but the cupboard was bare.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means affection shown only for what it will get you, like a pet's fondness at feeding time.

clue.text: Superior fur, not yet ready for being chucked out

definitions.text: not yet ready for being chucked out

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, a superior social register in British usage
sable is a prized fur from a small mammal

explanation.surface: A top-quality fur coat that isn't fit for throwing away yet.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from a 1950s British coinage about 'U and non-U' speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still serviceable is not ready for the bin, since it can still be put to work.

clue.text: Tom's about to go round Irish county

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
about signals turning things around, so the letters of Tom's are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s here supplies a letter
Erse is an old name for the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: Tom is on the point of touring an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles Tom's, and 'to go round' wraps that round the old word for Irish Gaelic. 'Irish county' tempts towards Ireland, but the answer is an English county in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county in the south-west, famous for cider and Cheddar.

clue.text: Unintelligible in company, he will get torn apart

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn apart

explanation.surface: In a firm, a man finds himself ripped to pieces and making no sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is confused and rambling cannot be understood, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: One may sit on the board of an eating establishment

definitions.text: One may sit on the board of an eating establishment

parts.words: One may sit on the board of an eating establishment
parts.note: reads like a company director at a restaurant chain, but the board is a wooden breadboard in a kitchen or dining room

explanation.surface: A director serving on the board of a restaurant company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a board of directors; it is the wooden board a loaf is cut on.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen blade for slicing loaves, which typically rests on the breadboard.

clue.text: Country lads getting nothing for duke

indicators.note: one letter is got in place of another, a swap
one letter is got in place of another, a swap

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Young men in a land lose their aristocrat and get nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked nation in South-East Asia bordering Vietnam and Thailand.

clue.text: They don't last long and may be thrown into mere heap

indicators.note: things thrown into a heap end up in a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Short-lived things may just be tossed onto a pile of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things of fleeting interest or use, like tickets and flyers, quickly discarded.

clue.text: A girl meeting a premature end unfortunately

indicators.note: the word stops short of its natural finish, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman dies too soon, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection expressing regret, the same sense as sadly.

clue.text: Increase gold given to American agents over time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over the next, so the agents come above time

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: Gold is handed to US agents over time, to boost their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men, short for government men, is American slang for FBI agents.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something larger or add to it, a synonym of boost.

clue.text: Child tucking into Lancashire dish, child making a mess

indicators.note: tucking into something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot is a lamb and potato stew from that northern English county
CH is the abbreviation for child, as in family trees
CH again stands for child

explanation.surface: A child digs into a stew while another makes a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating, but places the child inside the stew. Lancashire hotpot is a slow-baked stew of lamb topped with sliced potatoes, from that northern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumbled mixture or muddle of things, a synonym of hodgepodge.

clue.text: Bird nibbled morsel of bread maybe

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit is the past tense of bite, close to nibbled

explanation.surface: A bird pecked at a scrap of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty piece of food, of which a crumb of bread is one example.

clue.text: Party is loud — afternoon rest unable to begin

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: the word cannot start, so it loses its first letter

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: A party is noisy, so no one can start their afternoon nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, a Spanish-style carnival or party.

clue.text: Ready to drop, like a boxer?

definitions.meaning: a boxer is a breed of hound, so a weary one is a fatigued canine

explanation.surface: Exhausted, like a fighter at the end of a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' points to a fighter in the ring, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted means worn out, and a weary boxer is literally a fatigued hound.

clue.text: Character dispatched communication

definitions.meaning: a character can be a symbol of an alphabet, such as A or B
a written message sent by post

explanation.surface: A personality sent off a message.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a symbol of the alphabet; the other is a written message posted to someone.

clue.text: Box left over is incomplete

indicators.note: the word is not complete, missing its last letter

parts.note: spare means remaining, left over

explanation.surface: A container of leftovers is short of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container, but here it is the verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to practise boxing, trading punches in training.

clue.text: Fail to be alarmed?

parts.note: alarmed means woken by an alarm clock rather than frightened, so failing at that means staying in bed too long

explanation.surface: Not getting scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarmed' suggests fear, but it means roused by an alarm clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep past the time you meant to wake up, missing the alarm.

clue.text: Foreign ruler and queen going over motorway

indicators.note: the queen's letters straddle the road, going over it on each side

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A foreign potentate and the monarch drive over a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, from London to Leeds; the digit 1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince in parts of the Middle East and Africa.

clue.text: Someone who used to like farm vehicle's ventilation device

parts.note: an ex is someone who used to be a partner, a former one
a tractor is the workhorse vehicle on a farm
a fan is someone who likes a thing, an admirer

explanation.surface: A former admirer of tractors has a gadget for airing the cab.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally as an ex-fan with the farm vehicle placed inside; no word signals that, so the pieces are best taken in answer order: a former, the vehicle, an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised fan that pulls stale air or steam out of a kitchen or bathroom.
